Fit a log-concave factorization with automatic rank selection

Source: R/logconNMF.R, R/simultaneousNMF.R
logconNMF.Rd

Estimate ordered, nonnegative log-concave profiles and channel loadings from one signal or several related samples. The information criterion selects the number of components. Simultaneous fits share spectra while retaining the original scan grids and estimating a separate profile and area for each occurrence.

Usage

logconNMF(
  y,
  X = NULL,
  family = poisson("identity"),
  lambda = "gic",
  background = NULL,
  dispersion = NULL,
  theta = NULL,
  precluster = "auto",
  weights = NULL,
  offset = NULL,
  correlation = NULL,
  ncores = NULL,
  control = list(),
  start = NULL,
  path = NULL,
  align = TRUE,
  method = c("cosine", "hellinger"),
  verbose = FALSE
)

# S3 method for class 'logconNMF_fit'
coef(object, sample = NULL, normalize = c("none", "l1"), ...)

# S3 method for class 'logconNMF_fit'
fitted(object, sample = 1L, ...)

# S3 method for class 'simultaneousNMF'
plot(
  x,
  type = c("areas", "spectra", "profiles"),
  sample = NULL,
  compounds = seq_len(min(6L, nrow(x$P))),
  ...
)

sampleNMF(object, sample = 1L)

Arguments

y

A numeric scans-by-channels matrix or vector for one sample, or a list of at least two sample descriptions for a simultaneous fit. Each description contains y and increasing time, with optional X, background, fit, weights, offset, exposure, dispersion, theta, sample_id, group, small_width and edges. Supply observations, weights, offsets or initial fits as RDS paths to read them from disk. Samples share channel names and order. List names supply sample IDs when the descriptions omit sample_id.

X

Candidate profile matrix for a single sample, such as the sparse design from estimatePSF(). In a simultaneous fit, supply it in each sample description or let the simultaneous initializer estimate it.

family

Identity-link noise family: gaussian, poisson, quasipoisson, mgcv::nb, Gamma, nb1(), gammaScale() or gammaCensored(). The corresponding names, including "nb", "nb1" and "Gamma_scale", are also accepted. Count likelihoods require integer counts; quasipoisson accepts nonnegative intensities. Gaussian observations may be negative; their fitted latent signals remain nonnegative.

lambda

An information criterion ("gic", "aic", "bic", "ebic" or "mbic") or a nonnegative numeric penalty per selection degree of freedom, before any temporal information adjustment. With m channels, a single component incurs m * lambda; in a simultaneous fit a shared spectrum incurs (m - 1) * lambda and an occurrence incurs lambda.

background

Optional nonnegative scans-by-basis matrix, for example splines::bs(time, df=6, intercept=TRUE). Coefficients are nonnegative and unpenalized. NULL fits without a background.

dispersion

Known common Gaussian variance, quasipoisson scale, Gamma dispersion, NB1 variance-to-mean ratio or common Gamma scale. NULL estimates a pooled value from temporal differences and freezes it. Parameters supplied in a signal_families object are used when this argument is omitted. Poisson and NB2 use unit dispersion.

theta

NB2 shape, shared by all original channels. NULL estimates and freezes a temporal moment estimate; a positive value fixes it; a negative value initializes at its absolute value and enables pooled likelihood updates. A fixed shape in the supplied NB family is respected.

precluster

Maximum channel groups or a saved channelGroups() map. "auto" uses the original channels for a single sample and up to 32 common groups for a simultaneous fit. FALSE or NULL disables aggregation. Final fits use every original channel.

weights

Nonnegative likelihood weights: a scalar, row vector or matrix matching y. NULL uses one. Zero weights omit observations.

offset

Known nonnegative mean contribution, in the same supported formats as weights. NULL uses zero. It is included on the response scale because the link is identity.

correlation

Lag-one working information adjustment. NULL uses the fitter's default ("auto" for one sample and "none" for simultaneous fits), or control$correlation if supplied for a simultaneous fit.

ncores

Total core budget. NULL uses the detected physical core count. Simultaneous fits divide that budget between sample workers and their native threads, with one BLAS thread per worker.

control

Named controls. See splogconNMF() for one matrix. For a simultaneous fit, cycles=10L and initial_cycles=5L set refinement limits, rounds=3L sets the number of grouping rounds, and q=64L sets the local profile update resolution. The default rt_tolerance=NULL and alignment_window=NULL derive matching windows from the narrow-peak widths. ridge=TRUE checks the profile ridge across samples. The remaining defaults are censor=0.5, correlation="none", workers=NULL and cache=TRUE. initial=list() passes controls to the independent initial fits. workers limits concurrent samples within ncores. The cache stores aggregated observations in memory.

start

Optional list H, S and alpha, with original dimensions. H has scans in rows and compounds in columns; S has compounds in rows and all original channels in columns. alpha contains background coefficients and defaults to zero. Profiles are normalized with the inverse change applied to spectra. A restart bypasses initial screening and preclustering; nonnegative spectral entries can reopen during refitting.

path

New directory for the sample store and fitted factors in a simultaneous fit. NULL uses a temporary directory.

align

Estimate monotone time warps for a simultaneous fit.

method

Spectral distance for matching simultaneous samples, either "cosine" or "hellinger".

verbose

Print stage timings, objective changes and compound counts.

object

A fitted model returned by logconNMF(). sampleNMF() takes a simultaneous model.

sample

Sample index or ID. For a single matrix use 1L or "sample1". In coef(), NULL returns the common spectra for a simultaneous fit. In plot(), NULL displays all samples.

normalize

"none" returns amplitude-scaled loadings. "l1" returns unit-sum rows.

...

Further arguments passed to the underlying extractor.

x

A fitted simultaneous model for plotting.

type

Plot sample areas, common spectra or aligned compound profiles.

compounds

Compound indices to display in a simultaneous plot.

Value

A fitted object with estimated rank, the number of single-sample components or shared components. Use coef(), fitted() and GIC() in either mode. fitted() returns one sample on its original grid. A simultaneous fit includes consensus spectra P, sample-by-compound areas, compounds, alignment, paths, store, channel_groups and parallel thread allocation.

Details

Rank-selection objective. The fit approximately minimizes $$-2\sum_s \ell_{\nu_s}(M_s;Y_s) + \kappa\lambda d.$$ The weighted log-likelihood \(\ell_{\nu_s}\) uses the fitted mean \(M_s\) on the original channels of sample \(s\). For quasipoisson it is the Poisson log score divided by the sample's estimated or supplied dispersion. The optional working temporal adjustment is \(\kappa\), equal to one under independence. A numeric lambda sets the penalty per selection degree of freedom. The GIC preset uses \(\log(p)\log\log(n)\), with the PSF dictionary width and number of scans for a single matrix. For a sample list the preset uses \(p=n=\sum_s n_s\).

For one matrix with \(m\) channels and \(K\) components, \(d=mK\). For a simultaneous model, \(d=(m-1)G+L\), where \(G\) is the number of shared unit-sum spectra and \(L\) counts the detected sample–component occurrences. Each spectrum contributes \(m-1\) coordinates and each occurrence contributes one amplitude. Setting \(G=L=K\) gives the single-sample count. Profiles have contiguous support and a concave logarithm on the positive interval. Profile shapes and smooth backgrounds carry no additional rank charge.

The simultaneous objective and reported information criteria such as GIC() also count estimated noise parameters. The single-sample objective drops that constant charge for a fixed noise specification. Local refinement and fusion, deletion or addition of candidate components provide the approximate rank search. Final single-sample refinement also tries broader local starts for nearly coincident profiles, with acceptance checked on every original channel against the current fit and a refined control. This is enabled by default. For one matrix, control=list(profile_restarts=FALSE) disables the pass; simultaneous fits pass this option through control$initial.

For a simultaneous fit, put background, weights, offset and any initial fit in the sample descriptions. path = NULL uses a new temporary sample store. Supply a persistent path when saving a simultaneous fit for later use, and retain the store with the fitted object.

Numeric penalties in logconNMF() have the same scale in both modes. To reproduce a single-sample splogconNMF() call using a numeric compound penalty, divide that penalty by the number of channels.

Simultaneous models

Ignoring backgrounds, exposures and offsets, the sample means have the shared-factor form \(M_s = Q_s P\), with one common spectral factor \(P\) and sample-specific profile/area factors \(Q_s\). This follows the simultaneous-NMF terminology of Cichocki et al. (2009) and Lee et al. (2012). It does not introduce a separate cross-modality coupling matrix.

Samples can supply separate background bases, known exposures and noise parameters. With a time warp \(u=w_s(t)\), binwise Jacobian \(J\), and exposure \(e\), the fitted mean on the original grid is $$\mu_{sij}=e_{si}\{J_{si}\sum_g a_{sg}h_{sg}(u_{si})p_{gj} +(B_sA_s)_{ij}\}+o_{sij}.$$ Spectra sum to one and the profiles integrate to one on the aligned grid. Unit exposure models the supplied intensities. Use known integration durations as exposures for integrated counts. Scan spacing and small_width use the same time units.

Reciprocal spectral matches provide leading-edge alignment anchors. Compatible occurrences share spectra after checking overlap and profile shape in area order. At most one occurrence of a compound enters each sample. Local profile, spectral and background updates compare the full original-channel likelihood. Undetected occurrences have NA areas. Noise scales are held fixed when comparing groupings. A negative NB2 theta allows bounded, likelihood-improving shape updates.

The common channel map is learned from samples aggregated on common time bins. The fitter retains only the aggregated observations in its shared cache and reads the original channels in blocks from each sample store. Keep the store with the saved fitted object for reconstruction and plots.

Extract one sample

sampleNMF(object, sample) returns a single-sample factorization view. The view contains unit-sum original-grid profiles in H, matching amplitude-scaled spectra in S, its fitted background, integrated areas in integrated_area, and consensus IDs in compound_id. Alignment and exposure are included in the profiles and spectra. Use coef(), fitted() and GIC() on the returned view. The view carries no observed matrix.

Examples

X <- convMatrix(convKernel("gaussian", 9L), 50L)
signal <- cbind(700 * X[, 16L] + 350 * X[, 35L],
                150 * X[, 16L] + 500 * X[, 35L])
set.seed(12)
Y <- matrix(rpois(length(signal), signal), nrow(signal))
fit <- logconNMF(Y, X = X, ncores = 1L)
fit$rank
coef(fit, normalize = "l1")

second <- matrix(rpois(length(signal), 1.4 * signal), nrow(signal))
samples <- list(first = list(y = Y, time = seq_len(nrow(Y)), X = X),
  second = list(y = second, time = seq_len(nrow(Y)), X = X))
joint <- logconNMF(samples, ncores = 1L)
joint$rank
joint$areas
fitted(joint, sample = "second")[1:3, ]
second_fit <- sampleNMF(joint, sample = "second")
second_fit$compound_id
coef(second_fit)
